site.title: The Quesenberry & Harvey Family
site.subtitle: An American Story
site.tagline: Four centuries from the Virginia Tidewater to the Carolina Piedmont
site.intro: From the wooden ships that crossed the Atlantic in 1624, to the Highland Scots who landed at Wilmington in 1775, to the Confederate soldiers of Floyd County and the Wesleyan congregations of High Point — this is the chronicle of two families whose stories braid into the larger story of America itself.

people.name: Lonnie Olin Quesenberry
people.deathPlace: High Point, Guilford County, North Carolina
people.burial: Holly Hill Memorial Park, Thomasville, Davidson County, NC
people.epitaph: Born in the Tennessee hill country, came of age in the Norfolk shipyards on the eve of the Second World War, married Ruth Harvey in Greensboro, and lived out his life in High Point — three states in one American lifetime.

people.name: Ruth Garland Harvey Quesenberry
people.deathPlace: Shannon Gray Health Care, High Point, NC (age 90)
people.burial: Holly Hill Memorial Park, Thomasville, Davidson County, NC
people.epitaph: Valedictorian, lifelong cook, devoted mother — born when Calvin Coolidge was president, she lived through the second American century almost entire.

deathGeo.label: High Point, Guilford County, North Carolina

people.name: Esther Harvey Scott
people.burial: Shady Grove Wesleyan Church Cemetery, Colfax, Guilford County, NC
people.epitaph: Ruth's younger sister — born in Colfax, married just before Ruth, served as a private-duty and office nurse in Kernersville for most of her life.

people.name: Anderson L. Scott
people.epitaph: Esther's husband — named in her 2021 obituary; further details await further research.

people.name: Floyd Harmon Quesenberry
people.epitaph: Born of the old Floyd County Virginia Quesenberry line, raised his sons in Tennessee and the Norfolk shipyards, and lived to see Lonnie's grandchildren — eighty-five years across three states.

people.name: Eva Elizabeth Mullins Quesenberry
people.epitaph: Maiden name Mullins — not Quesenberry. Lonnie's mother lived to the age of ninety-two, outliving her husband by thirteen years and her own century almost entire.

people.name: William Carl Harvey
people.epitaph: Ruth and Esther's father — first name was William, called Carl. Colfax farmer, Wesleyan churchman, husband of Geneva McMichael for forty-seven years.

people.name: Geneva Esther McMicheal Harvey
people.epitaph: Geneva Esther — daughter of William Franklin McMichael of Deep River, Guilford County. Married William Carl Harvey on a June day in 1919 and outlived him by five years.

people.name: William Henry Clay Quesenberry
people.epitaph: Born in a Blue Ridge hollow, named for a Whig statesman, fought for the Confederacy, died in the Arizona desert. One of nine brothers in the same gray uniform.
people.military: American Civil War — Confederate Army (one of the famous nine sons)

people.name: Eva Jane Slusher Quesenberry
people.epitaph: Granddaughter of a Pennsylvania-German DAR Patriot, daughter of the Slushers and the Hyltons of Indian Valley, wife of one of the nine Confederate Quesenberrys. She lived from Andrew Jackson to Calvin Coolidge.

people.name: John Quesenberry Sr.
people.epitaph: Patriarch of Greasy Creek — and, by Civil War's end, the only American father documented to have sent nine sons into Confederate service.

people.name: George Quesenberry
people.deathPlace: Floyd County (then part of Montgomery County), Virginia
people.epitaph: American Revolutionary soldier, frontier settler — he carried the Quesenberry name from the colonial Tidewater into the Blue Ridge.
people.military: American Revolutionary War — Montgomery County, Virginia Militia

people.name: Aaron Quisenberry Sr.
people.deathPlace: St. Thomas Parish, Orange County, Virginia
people.epitaph: DAR Patriot Ancestor #A093307 — furnished beef to Washington's Continental Army from his Orange County, Virginia farm.
people.military: American Revolution — DAR Patriot Ancestor #A093307; furnished beef to the Continental Army

people.name: Thomas Questenbury
people.epitaph: The Atlantic crossing of 1624 — Thomas Questenbury, sixteen years old, a passenger to colonial Virginia. From him every American Quesenberry, Quisenberry, and Christenberry descends.

people.name: John Quisenberry Sr.
people.epitaph: First American-born Quisenberry — planter of Westmoreland County, husband of Anne Pope, by marriage a distant cousin of George Washington.

people.name: Christopher Slusher (Schlosser)
people.epitaph: Revolutionary War soldier from Lancaster County, Pennsylvania — DAR Patriot Ancestor #A105465 — and the German-American great-grandfather of Eva Jane Slusher.
people.military: American Revolution — DAR Patriot Ancestor #A105465 (Pennsylvania service)

people.name: Billie R. Quesenberry
people.epitaph: Lonnie's sibling — appears in the 1940 federal census household at Western Branch, Norfolk, Virginia. Birth, death, and full name await further research.

people.name: Alexander Henry Quesenberry, Jr.
people.deathPlace: University of Virginia Hospital, Charlottesville, Virginia
people.epitaph: Born the year his father died at Gettysburg's bloody summer — raised by his widowed mother Rebecca Smyth — lived seventy-four years across Reconstruction and the Industrial Age.

people.name: Matilda Jane Price Quesenberry
people.epitaph: Wife of Alexander Henry Quesenberry, Jr.; mother of Floyd. Daughter of Alexander Stewart Price (1833–1909). Lived from Reconstruction through the Second World War.

people.name: Pvt. Alexander Henry Quesenberry, Sr.
people.deathPlace: Battle of Chancellorsville, Spotsylvania County, Virginia
people.epitaph: Killed at Chancellorsville on the third of May, 1863 — the same battle that mortally wounded Stonewall Jackson. His widow Rebecca was carrying their son when he died; the boy was born three months later.
people.military: Confederate Private — KILLED IN ACTION at the Battle of Chancellorsville, 3 May 1863. Aged 21.

people.name: Rebecca Jane Smyth Quesenberry Travis
people.epitaph: Widowed at nineteen by the Civil War. Buried two husbands and raised at least seven children. Lived to see her grandson Floyd come of age.

people.name: Crockett Quisenberry
people.epitaph: Lived from Andrew Jackson's first term to the dawn of Theodore Roosevelt's century. Saw the Civil War take his son.

people.name: Nancy J. Quesenberry
people.epitaph: Wife of Crockett Quisenberry. Her surname Quesenberry suggests she may have been a cousin — common in the heavily intermarried Floyd County hollows.

people.name: James S. Quesenberry
people.epitaph: Born the year George Washington gave his Farewell Address, dead the year America declared war on Mexico. A southwest Virginia farmer.

people.name: Elizabeth Moore Quesenberry
people.epitaph: Born with the new century, daughter of Peter Moore Sr., Pvt.

people.name: George S. Quesenberry
people.epitaph: Brother or close kin of James S. Quesenberry. The two men's nearly identical lifespans suggest twins or close brothers.

people.name: Mary Quesenberry
people.epitaph: Wife of George S. Quesenberry. Maiden name not yet recovered.

people.name: Peter Moore Sr.
people.epitaph: Pvt. Peter Moore Sr. — the rank in his recorded name marks him as a soldier of the early Republic.
people.military: Recorded as 'Pvt.' — likely Revolutionary War or War of 1812 service

people.name: Jane 'Jeany' Murtland Moore
people.epitaph: Wife of Pvt. Peter Moore Sr. Her surname Murtland is Scots-Irish — pointing to the Ulster-Scot migrations.

people.name: James Calloway Mullins
people.deathPlace: Yokum Station District, Lee County, Virginia
people.epitaph: Born March 1854 in Hancock County, Tennessee; died 1929 in Lee County, Virginia. Father of Eva Mullins. Of the great Mullins clan of the Cumberland Gap.

people.name: Annis Stapleton Mullins
people.epitaph: Mother of Eva Elizabeth Mullins. Daughter of Robert Thomas Stapleton (1830–1911) and Nancy Jane Winstead (b. 1841).

people.name: Isaac J. Harvey
people.deathPlace: Deep River, Guilford County, North Carolina
people.burial: 13 April 1912, Deep River, Guilford County, NC
people.epitaph: Widowed twice before he married Ruth's grandmother. Father of seven across three marriages, including a Wesleyan minister.

people.name: Rachel Frances Swift Harvey
people.epitaph: Mother of William Carl Harvey. Daughter of Thomas S. Swift and Lucinda Cox (1822–1889).

people.name: William Franklin McMichael
people.epitaph: Father of Geneva — born in 1849 (the year of the California Gold Rush), died in April 1941 at ninety-one or ninety-two, just months before Pearl Harbor. Son of Jesse C. McMichael (1820–1907).

people.name: Sally Pegram McMichael
people.epitaph: Mother of Geneva McMichael Harvey. Daughter of James Fletcher Pegram (1831–1915) of the Piedmont Pegram family.

people.name: Anthony Harvey
people.epitaph: Father of Isaac J. Harvey. Of the colonial-era Quaker Harveys of North Carolina (per the Trueblood spousal connection).

people.name: Sarah Sally Trueblood Harvey
people.epitaph: Of the colonial Quaker Trueblood family of North Carolina. Mother of Isaac J. Harvey.

people.name: Thomas S. Swift
people.epitaph: Father of Rachel Frances Swift Harvey. Of the Piedmont North Carolina Swift family.

people.name: Lucinda Cox Swift
people.epitaph: Wife of Thomas S. Swift, mother of Rachel. Born under James Monroe, died at sixty-seven under Benjamin Harrison.

people.name: James Fletcher Pegram
people.deathPlace: Deep River Township, Guilford County, North Carolina
people.epitaph: Father of Sally Pegram, grandfather of Geneva. Married 1853 in Forsyth County, lived eighty-four years through the Civil War, Reconstruction, and the start of the Great War.

people.name: Annie Elizabeth Gates Pegram
people.epitaph: Wife of James Fletcher Pegram, mother of Sally. Five years older than her husband — unusual for the era.

people.name: Jesse C. McMichael
people.epitaph: Father of William Franklin McMichael, grandfather of Geneva. His mother was a Pegram, his son's wife was a Pegram — the McMichael-Pegram intermarriage runs at least three generations deep in Deep River.

people.name: Anna Stephens McMichael
people.epitaph: Wife of Jesse C. McMichael, mother of William Franklin McMichael, grandmother of Geneva.

people.name: Alexander Stewart Price
people.epitaph: Father of Matilda Jane Price, grandfather of Floyd Harmon Quesenberry. Lived seventy-six years through the Civil War, Reconstruction, and the Wright Brothers' first flight.

people.name: Martha Jane Collins Price
people.epitaph: Wife of Alexander Stewart Price, mother of Matilda Jane Price.

people.name: Robert Thomas Stapleton
people.epitaph: Father of Annis Stapleton, grandfather of Eva Mullins. Lived eighty-one years through the Civil War, Reconstruction, and the dawn of the automobile age.

people.name: Nancy Jane Winstead Stapleton
people.epitaph: Wife of Robert Thomas Stapleton, mother of Annis. Born the year of William Henry Harrison's brief presidency.

people.name: Judith Deuce Osborne Harvey
people.epitaph: Born in Staffordshire, England in 1683. Emigrated to William Penn's colony, married twice, bore at least ten children, lived to eighty-seven. The deepest English-born ancestor in this tree.

people.name: William HARVEY (colonial)
people.epitaph: Colonial-era Harvey patriarch. Married Judith ca. 1715; from him descend the American Harveys of this line.

people.name: Nathaniel Newlin
people.epitaph: Pennsylvania Quaker — son of an Irish Quaker emigrant who came to Penn's colony in 1683. The deepest Quaker-side ancestor on this site.

people.name: Jane Newlin
people.epitaph: Pennsylvania Quaker. Wife of Nathaniel Newlin.

people.name: Mary Glendenning Hoggatt
people.deathPlace: Deep River, Guilford County, North Carolina
people.burial: Springfield Friends Meeting, Guilford County, NC
people.epitaph: Born in Edinburgh, Scotland in 1698. Crossed the Atlantic as a young woman, married a Quaker in colonial America, lived to eighty-two, and was buried at Springfield Friends Meeting in North Carolina.

people.name: Philip Hoggett
people.epitaph: Husband of Mary Hoggatt. Colonial Quaker patriarch of this Hoggatt-Harvey line.

people.name: Harrison Mullins
people.epitaph: Father of James Calloway Mullins. Lived ninety-one years from Andrew Jackson to Warren G. Harding; saw his son grow old.

people.name: Manerva Jane Mullins
people.epitaph: Of the Claiborne County, Tennessee Mullins families. Mother of James Calloway Mullins.

people.name: Hiram Mullins
people.epitaph: Father of Harrison Mullins. Born in North Carolina under George Washington's second term; died in Tennessee just before the Civil War.

people.name: Nancy Orlenia Singleton Mullins
people.epitaph: Wife of Hiram Mullins. Migrated west from Tennessee to Arkansas in her later years — died in Izard County, Arkansas.

people.name: Nathan Heaver Harvey
people.epitaph: Pennsylvania Quaker, born in William Penn's colony at the eve of the Revolution. Migrated south to Orange County, NC, where he died at seventy-seven.

people.name: Agnes Harvey
people.deathPlace: Spring Friends Burial Grounds, Orange County, North Carolina
people.epitaph: Born Christmas Day 1756 in Rowan County, NC. Buried at Spring Friends Burial Grounds — a confirmed Quaker resting place.

people.name: Isaac L. Harvey
people.epitaph: Born at Chadds Ford in 1718 — site of the 1777 Battle of Brandywine — and lived 84 years, witnessing the founding of the United States.

people.name: Martha E. Newlin Harvey
people.epitaph: Born Newlin in colonial Pennsylvania, married Harvey, migrated south to North Carolina. The bridge between two Quaker emigrant lines.

people.name: Anthony P. Hoggatt
people.epitaph: Of the Cedar Creek, Virginia Quaker community. Lived 84 years from George II to James Madison.

people.name: Mary Agnes Stanley Hoggatt
people.epitaph: Born MARY AGNES STANLEY in Hanover County VA — not a Hoggatt by birth, as her name in our tree might suggest. She married Anthony P. Hoggatt and took his surname.

people.name: Riley James Mullins
people.deathPlace: Rock Island Confederate POW Camp, Rock Island, Illinois
people.epitaph: Captured Confederate soldier from Claiborne County, Tennessee. Died as a prisoner of war at Rock Island, Illinois — ten months after his cousin Pvt. Alexander Henry Quesenberry Sr. fell at Chancellorsville.
people.military: Confederate soldier — died as a prisoner of war at the Rock Island, Illinois POW camp, 16 February 1864

deathGeo.label: Rock Island Confederate POW Camp, Illinois

people.name: Edward McDonald Smyth
people.epitaph: Father of Rebecca Jane Smyth — the young Lee County widow of Pvt. Alexander Henry Quesenberry Sr.

people.name: Minerva Parsons Smyth
people.epitaph: Mother of Rebecca Jane Smyth.

people.name: James T. Travis
people.epitaph: Rebecca Jane Smyth's second husband. After her Confederate-soldier first husband was killed at Chancellorsville, she remarried Travis and bore at least five more children with him.

people.name: Mary E. Quesenberry Graham
people.epitaph: The previously unknown sister of Alexander Henry Quesenberry Jr. — the daughter Rebecca was probably carrying when her husband died at Chancellorsville, or born shortly after.

people.name: Jesse Pegram
people.epitaph: Father of James Fletcher Pegram, grandfather of Sally, great-grandfather of Geneva. Of the Forsyth-Rockingham-Guilford Pegram family.

people.name: Lucretia Juanita Fuller Pegram
people.epitaph: Mother of James Fletcher Pegram. Maiden name Fuller — an English Piedmont surname.

people.name: William Aydlott McMichael, Sr.
people.epitaph: Patriarch of the McMichaels of Guilford County. Husband of Rhoda Pegram — and thus the first generation to begin the Pegram-McMichael intermarriage that would define three generations of Deep River kinship.

people.name: Rhoda E. Pegram McMichael
people.epitaph: The bridge between the Pegram and McMichael families. Her marriage to William Aydlott McMichael Sr. began three generations of intermarriage in Deep River.

people.name: David George Glendenning
people.epitaph: Edinburgh-born father of Mary Glendenning Hoggatt. The deepest known Scottish ancestor in this tree.

people.name: Margaret Hall Glendenning
people.epitaph: Edinburgh-born mother of Mary Glendenning Hoggatt.

people.name: Samuel Deuce
people.epitaph: Father of Judith Deuce Osborne Harvey, born Bilston, Staffordshire. The deepest English-born ancestor in this tree.

people.name: Elizabeth Deuce
people.epitaph: Mother of Judith Deuce Osborne Harvey. Maiden name not yet recovered.

people.name: Catherine "Rachel" Hutchins Stanley
people.deathPlace: Guilford, North Carolina, British Colonial America
people.burial: New Garden Friends Monthly Meeting, Guilford County, NC
people.epitaph: Born Henrico, Virginia 1703. Married James Stanley 1728. Buried at New Garden Friends Meeting in Guilford NC, 1766. The deepest Hutchins-Stanley ancestor on the Harvey side.

people.name: James Stanley, Sr.
people.epitaph: Husband of Catherine Hutchins Stanley. Together they raised eight children in colonial Virginia and migrated south to North Carolina.

people.name: Nicholas Hutchins
people.epitaph: Father of Catherine Hutchins Stanley, patriarch of the Hutchins line in colonial Henrico, Virginia.

people.name: Mary Watkins Hutchins
people.epitaph: Mother of Catherine Hutchins Stanley. Of the Watkins family of colonial Henrico, Virginia.
